question: Which of the following options in PowerPoint allows you to see all the slides at once as thumbnails?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Slide Sorter View**__.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Slide Sorter View** in Microsoft PowerPoint displays all slides in a presentation as thumbnails, allowing users to easily rearrange, delete, or apply transitions between slides.
 
• This view provides a **bird's-eye view of the entire presentation**, making it easier to organize slides and review the flow of content.
 
• Slide Sorter View is **especially useful for large presentations** with numerous slides, as it enables quick identification and movement of specific slides.
 
• It can be accessed from the **View tab** on the Ribbon or by clicking on the Slide Sorter icon in the bottom-right corner of the PowerPoint interface.
 
• In this view, users can also apply **slide transitions** to multiple slides simultaneously by selecting them and using the Transitions tab.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

 
• **Outline View**

 
 
• Outline View displays the text content of the slides in a hierarchical structure without showing visual elements such as images or designs.
 
• This view is useful for focusing on the content and structure of the presentation.
 
 
 
• **Reading View**
 
 
• Reading View allows users to preview how the presentation will appear in full screen but within the PowerPoint window itself.
 
• It is designed for reviewing presentations without the need to start the Slide Show mode.
 
 
 
• **Slide Show View**
 
 
• Slide Show View runs the presentation in full-screen mode, displaying slides sequentially with applied animations and transitions.
 
• This is the view used during an actual presentation to an audience.
 
 
 
• **Normal View**
 
 
• Normal View is the default view in PowerPoint, where users can edit slides, add content, and view the slide pane, notes pane, and slide thumbnails simultaneously.
 
• It provides a detailed workspace for creating and customizing individual slides.
